beats.text: How do you lift a road out of a ship's way? The secret is hiding behind the hinge.
First, traffic stops and the barriers close. The moving section must be clear before it opens.
This bascule bridge turns around a fixed steel pivot, just like a giant seesaw.
A heavy counterweight sits behind that pivot. As the road rises, the weight swings down into its chamber.
The counterweight balances much of the road's weight. A motor and gears control the movement instead of lifting everything alone.
With the road raised, the tall ship can pass through the open channel.
Once the ship is clear, the drive lowers the road. The counterweight swings back up.
The span seats and locks, then traffic resumes. One balanced mechanism makes room for two kinds of journey.
